title: A procedural plinth stone
note: The marble the Projects Panel's plinth is cut from, generated rather than photographed: a black ground under three sets of level-set veins with a fracture network over the top, rendered in Cycles to one 3000 by 269 plate. What it CANNOT make is a branching vein - docs/agents/plinth-marble.md has the measurement - which is what the photographic Bake beside this one is for.
needs: Blender on PATH, with Cycles. Fifteen seconds a stone on a GPU and a few minutes without one.

groups.name: What is being baked
groups.note: This Bake IS one stone. Its parameters are read straight out of this recipe by build-slab.py - see tuned_stone() there - and merged in beside the four built-in candidates, so nothing downstream knows the difference. It renders that one stone and never a built-in: the four procedural plates and the four gemini ones are the recorded marble comparison, and re-rendering them would overwrite the pictures it was judged from, so a name this file already defines is refused rather than shadowed.

params.label: the stone's name
params.note: Lower case, digits and dashes. `nero`, `portoro`, `marquina`, `arabescato`, any gemini plate and any -noir twin of one are refused by the generator - it says so and renders nothing.

params.label: what it is
params.note: One line, shown beside its plate in the picker.

groups.name: The ground
groups.note: A reference slab of Portoro is very nearly black between its seams and its calcite is very nearly white - the stone is almost all contrast. A lifted floor under lowered veins is exactly how stone comes out looking like dusty concrete.

params.label: the black
params.note: Linear, and much darker than it looks written down: the built-in Portoro's ground is 0.0052 of full, which is this. Written as sRGB and decoded to linear on the way in, because the numbers this generator works in run below 1/255 and a hex digit cannot say 0.0052 - see design/bake/tuning.py, which is where the one conversion lives.

params.label: base roughness
params.note: The polish on the ground itself. The plinth is a polished slab, so this is low and every seam below is rougher than it.

groups.name: Veins - the swathe
groups.note: The broadest set: in Portoro this is the gold, and it is a swathe rather than a filament.

params.label: scale
params.note: How many times the noise field repeats across the block. Higher is a finer network.

params.label: detail
params.note: Octaves of the field. More is a busier, more fractal edge to every vein.

params.label: distortion
params.note: How far the field is warped before the level is taken - what stops a vein reading as a contour line.

params.label: width
params.note: The level the vein is cut at, so how wide a seam is as a share of the field.

params.label: sharpness
params.note: How abruptly the seam's edge falls off. High is a hairline; low is a bruise.

params.label: colour
params.note: The seam's own colour, before the room lights it. Written as sRGB and decoded to linear on the way in, because the numbers this generator works in run below 1/255 and a hex digit cannot say 0.0052 - see design/bake/tuning.py, which is where the one conversion lives.

params.label: roughness
params.note: The seam's polish against the ground's. A calcite seam is not as polished as the black around it.

params.label: bump
params.note: How far the seam stands off the surface. This is relief and not colour.

groups.name: Veins - the network
groups.note: The middle set, which is what makes the stone read as branching rather than as stripes.

groups.name: The fracture
groups.note: Cracks post-date everything, so they are laid last - which is also the right geology. Crisper than a JPEG can hold at this magnification, which is the one thing the procedural generator does that a photograph cannot.

params.label: colour
params.note: The crack's own colour. Written as sRGB and decoded to linear on the way in, because the numbers this generator works in run below 1/255 and a hex digit cannot say 0.0052 - see design/bake/tuning.py, which is where the one conversion lives.

params.label: roughness
params.note: As a vein's.

params.label: bump
params.note: As a vein's.

params.label: strength
params.note: How much of the network is laid down at all. 0 is no cracks.

groups.name: The render
groups.note: Cycles. Fifteen seconds a stone on a GPU at the sample count below, and roughly linear in it.

params.label: samples
params.note: Path-traced samples per pixel. Halving this halves the render, and shows as noise in the polish before it shows anywhere else.

params.label: seed
params.note: Any constant will do; changing it moves where every vein falls without changing what kind of stone it is.

params.label: the room
params.note: Which surround it is lit in. `flat` is the fitted one every stone in the file uses; the others are the lighting question rather than the marble one. A light reads as a highlight or as a veil depending on its ANGULAR size against the plus or minus fourteen degrees the front face sweeps - docs/agents/plinth-marble.md carries that, and it is the rule that cost three wrong diagnoses.
